rule_text: You must offer tools for account holders to manage their privacy and account settings; for account holders under thirteen years of age, these tools must also be offered to their parents or guardians, and for minor account holders thirteen and older, related tools must be offered to parents or guardians as appropriate based on relevant risks.

rule_text: The Attorney General must post on their website information about controller and processor responsibilities, consumer rights under the Act, and provide an online complaint submission mechanism.
rule_text_technical: The Attorney General shall post on the Attorney General's website: (1) information relating to (a) the responsibilities of a controller, (b) the responsibilities of a processor, and (c) a consumer's rights under the Agricultural Data Privacy Act; and (2) an online mechanism through which a person may submit a complaint under the Agricultural Data Privacy Act to the Attorney General.

rule_text: You are not required to apply data privacy protections to information about government officers or employees that relates to their position or functions, such as their title, business address, office telephone number, salary range, or name on official documents.
rule_text_technical: This Act does not apply to information about any individual who is or was an officer or employee of a government institution that relates to the position or functions of the individual, including the fact of employment, title, business address, office telephone number, classification, salary range and responsibilities of the position held, and the name of the individual on a document prepared in the course of employment.

rule_text: You must carry out assessments related to the user empowerment duty under Section 15(2) for your regulated user-to-user service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to a duty to conduct assessments as specified in Section 14, in connection with the user empowerment duty set out in Section 15(2).

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must implement user empowerment measures on your regulated user-to-user service, giving users tools to control their online experience.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to enforceable user empowerment duties under Section 15, requiring the provision of tools and functionalities that enable users to manage and control content they encounter on the service.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must have systems to protect news publisher content from undue removal or restriction on your regulated user-to-user service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to a duty under Section 18 in relation to news publisher content, requiring systems and processes that protect such content from disproportionate removal or restriction.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must provide users with accessible mechanisms to report harmful or illegal content on your regulated user-to-user service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to a content reporting duty under Section 20, requiring the provision of clear and accessible means by which users can report content that they consider to be harmful or illegal.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must operate effective complaints procedures allowing users to challenge decisions made about content on your regulated user-to-user service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to an enforceable duty under Section 21 to operate adequate complaints procedures enabling users and affected persons to seek redress in relation to content decisions made by the provider.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must have regard to freedom of expression and privacy when implementing your safety duties on your regulated user-to-user service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to a duty under Section 22 to protect users' right to freedom of expression and privacy when designing and implementing the systems, processes, and measures required under Part 3 of the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

instances.citation: Schedule 2 — Serious invasions of privacy (Public interest balancing)
instances.notes: Both require balancing privacy against freedom of expression and other public interests, but the Australian rule applies to judicial determination of privacy tort claims while the UK rule applies to platform operators implementing safety duties.

rule_text: You must keep records of your risk assessments, safety measures, and compliance activities, and review them regularly on your regulated user-to-user service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated user-to-user services are subject to a duty under Section 23 to maintain records of their risk assessments and related documentation, and to conduct periodic reviews of those assessments and the measures taken in response.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must conduct illegal content risk assessments for your regulated search service as required under the Act.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to a duty under Section 26 to carry out illegal content risk assessments in accordance with the requirements specified by OFCOM.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must take steps to address illegal content returned in search results on your regulated search service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to enforceable duties under Section 27 concerning illegal content in search results, requiring implementation of systems and processes to identify and mitigate the presentation of illegal content.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must conduct children's risk assessments for your regulated search service to identify risks of harm to children from search results.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to a duty under Section 28 to carry out children's risk assessments, evaluating the risks of harm to children arising from the operation of their search service.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must implement duties relating to children's online safety on your regulated search service to protect children from harmful search results.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to enforceable duties under Section 29 concerning children's online safety, requiring systems and processes to protect children from encountering harmful content through search results.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must provide users with accessible mechanisms to report harmful or illegal search results on your regulated search service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to a content reporting duty under Section 31, requiring the provision of clear and accessible means by which users can report search results that they consider to be harmful or illegal.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must operate effective complaints procedures for users of your regulated search service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to a duty under Section 32 to operate adequate complaints procedures enabling users and affected persons to raise concerns and seek redress regarding the search service.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must keep records of your risk assessments, safety measures, and compliance activities, and review them regularly on your regulated search service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to a duty under Section 34 to maintain records of their risk assessments and related documentation, and to conduct periodic reviews of those assessments and the measures implemented in response.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must conduct children's access assessments to determine whether children are likely to access your service, where required under the Act.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services that may be accessed by children are subject to a duty under Section 36 to carry out children's access assessments to determine whether their service is likely to be accessed by children, in accordance with the methodology and requirements specified by OFCOM.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must implement measures to prevent fraudulent advertising from appearing on your regulated service, as required under the Act.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services falling within the scope of Section 38 are subject to an enforceable duty to implement systems and processes designed to identify and prevent the publication or display of fraudulent advertising on their services.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must take steps to address fraudulent advertising on search results within your regulated search service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated search services are subject to a duty under Section 39 to implement systems and processes to prevent the appearance of fraudulent advertising within search results, in accordance with the requirements of the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must implement user identity verification systems on your service where required by OFCOM or where you choose to offer this functionality.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services are subject to duties under Section 64 relating to user identity verification, requiring the implementation of systems enabling users to verify their identity or, where required by OFCOM, to make such verification available or mandatory.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You may only take action against users on your service in accordance with your published terms of service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services are subject to a duty under Section 71 to act against users only in ways that are consistent with and authorised by their published terms of service, ensuring that enforcement actions against users are grounded in those terms.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: Your terms of service must meet the standards required by the Act, including being clear, accessible, and compliant with the duties imposed on your service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services are subject to enforceable requirements under Section 72 that their terms of service must satisfy, including that such terms are clear, accessible to users, and consistent with the duties and obligations imposed on the provider under the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must provide information about a deceased child user's use of your service to their parent or guardian upon a valid request.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services are subject to a duty under Section 75 to supply information about the use of the service by a deceased child user to a qualifying person (such as a parent or guardian), upon receipt of a valid request made in accordance with the requirements of the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must produce and publish transparency reports about your service's compliance with your safety duties, in the format and at the frequency required by OFCOM.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services falling within the scope of Section 77(3) and (4) are subject to obligations to produce transparency reports containing information specified by OFCOM regarding their compliance with their duties under the Act, and to publish those reports in accordance with OFCOM's requirements.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

instances.citation: Ch. 501, Part V, F.S. — Special Obligations for Large Online Platforms (Transparency Reports)
instances.notes: Both require large platforms to publish transparency reports, but Florida's requirement is specific to qualifying large online platforms and covers content moderation practices, while the UK rule applies to regulated services under OFCOM's framework.

rule_text: You must comply with the duties relating to provider pornographic content on your regulated service, including ensuring appropriate protections are in place.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services hosting provider pornographic content are subject to enforceable duties under Section 81 requiring them to implement appropriate systems, processes, and protections in relation to such content, in accordance with the requirements of Part 5 of the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must notify OFCOM when you become liable to pay fees under the Act's fee-charging regime.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services that become subject to the fee-charging provisions of Part 6 of the Act are required under Section 83 to notify OFCOM of this fact, in accordance with the notification requirements and timescales specified under the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must comply with information notices issued to you by OFCOM requesting information relevant to the performance of its online safety functions.
rule_text_technical: Persons or providers who receive an information notice issued by OFCOM under Section 102 are subject to a binding obligation under Section 102(8) to comply with that notice, providing the information requested within the timeframes and in the manner specified therein.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must provide assistance to a skilled person appointed by OFCOM to carry out an audit or review of your service.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services are subject to a duty under Section 104(7) to provide assistance and cooperation to a skilled person appointed by OFCOM to undertake an audit, review, or assessment of the provider's service or compliance with its duties under the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

rule_text: You must cooperate with any investigation being conducted by OFCOM into your service's compliance with the Act.
rule_text_technical: Providers of regulated services and other relevant persons are subject to an enforceable duty under Section 105(1) to cooperate with any investigation conducted by OFCOM in connection with the exercise of its online safety functions, including by providing information, access, and assistance as required.

first_instance.law_name: Online Safety Act 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UK Online Safety Act 2023 (United Kingdom, 2023-10-26).

Both require cooperation with investigation by a supervisory authority, but Kenya's rule is data-protection specific while the UK Online Safety Act provision concerns OFCOM investigations into platform compliance.

rule_text: You must display an identification containing the name and address of the person paying for any billboard, placard, poster, pamphlet, or other printed matter referencing an election, candidate, or ballot question.
rule_text_technical: Except as otherwise provided and subject to subsections (3) and (4), a billboard, placard, poster, pamphlet, or other printed matter having reference to an election, a candidate, or a ballot question must display an identification containing the name and address of the person paying for the matter.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must ensure any paid radio or television advertisement referencing an election, candidate, or ballot question identifies the sponsoring person as required by the FCC, bears the name of the person paying for it, and complies with subsection (3).
rule_text_technical: A radio or television paid advertisement having reference to an election, a candidate, or a ballot question must identify the sponsoring person as required by the Federal Communications Commission, bear an identification that contains the name of the person paying for the advertisement, and be in compliance with subsection (3) and, except as otherwise provided by subsection (5), with the disclaimers specified in subsections (2)(a) and (2)(b).

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must include the disclaimer 'Not authorized by any candidate' on any paid radio or television advertisement relating to a candidate that constitutes an independent expenditure.
rule_text_technical: If the radio or television paid advertisement relates to a candidate and is an independent expenditure, the advertisement must contain the disclaimer: 'Not authorized by any candidate'.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must include an authorization disclaimer naming the candidate or candidate committee on any paid radio or television advertisement relating to a candidate that is not an independent expenditure but is paid for by someone other than that candidate.
rule_text_technical: If the radio or television paid advertisement relates to a candidate and is not an independent expenditure but is paid for by a person other than the candidate to which it is related, the advertisement must contain the disclaimer: 'Authorized by [name of candidate or name of candidate committee]'.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: The size and placement of any required identification or disclaimer must comply with rules promulgated by the Secretary of State, which may exempt items such as campaign buttons or balloons where adding identification is unreasonable.
rule_text_technical: The size and placement of an identification or disclaimer required by this section must be determined by rules promulgated by the secretary of state. The rules may exempt printed matter and certain other items such as campaign buttons or balloons, the size of which makes it unreasonable to add an identification or disclaimer, from the identification or disclaimer required by this section.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must include the statement 'with regulated funds' in each identification on printed matter or radio or television paid advertisements, unless the communication falls under the exemption in subsection (5) or is a candidate committee's own material.
rule_text_technical: Except for a communication described in subsection (5) and except for a candidate committee's printed matter or radio or television paid advertisements, each identification required by this section must also indicate that the printed matter or radio or television paid advertisement is paid for 'with regulated funds'. Printed matter or a radio or television paid advertisement not subject to this act must not bear this statement.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must include the required identification if your otherwise-exempt communication references a clearly identified candidate or ballot question within 60 days before a general election or 30 days before a primary election and is targeted to the relevant electorate via radio, television, mass mailing, or prerecorded telephone message.
rule_text_technical: A communication otherwise entirely exempted from this act under section 6(2)(j) must contain the identification required by subsection (1), (2), or (7) if that communication references a clearly identified candidate or ballot question within 60 days before a general election or 30 days before a primary election in which the candidate or ballot question appears on a ballot and is targeted to the relevant electorate by means of radio, television, mass mailing, or prerecorded telephone message.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You are not required to include the disclaimer otherwise mandated under subsection (1) or (2) for communications described in subsection (5).
rule_text_technical: A communication described in subsection (5) is not required to contain the disclaimer required under subsection (1) or (2).

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You can be found guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to $1,000 or imprisonment of up to 93 days or both, if you knowingly violate this section.
rule_text_technical: A person who knowingly violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than $1,000.00 or imprisonment for not more than 93 days, or both.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must include the name, telephone number, address, or other contact information of the person paying for any prerecorded telephone message that expressly advocates for or against a clearly identified candidate or ballot question, and must comply with the 'regulated funds' identification requirement.
rule_text_technical: A prerecorded telephone message that in express terms advocates the election or defeat of a clearly identified candidate, or the qualification, passage, or defeat of a ballot question, must bear an identification that contains the name and telephone number, address, or other contact information of the person paying for the prerecorded telephone message, and must be in compliance with subsection (4).

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: The required disclosure statement in a qualified political advertisement must state that the advertisement was generated in whole or substantially by artificial intelligence.
rule_text_technical: The disclosure statement required in a qualified political advertisement must state that the qualified political advertisement was generated in whole or substantially by artificial intelligence.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

instances.citation: CS/HB 919 / ch. 2024-126 — Disclosure Requirement (Printed/Digital Graphic Format)
instances.notes: Both require a disclosure statement on printed or digital political communications containing AI-generated content; Florida specifies the exact disclaimer text while Michigan also mandates specific disclosure language.

rule_text: If the qualified political advertisement is a video communication with audio, the AI disclosure must be in the same language as the language used in the video communication.
rule_text_technical: If the qualified political advertisement is a video communication that also includes audio, the required disclosure must be in the same language as the language used in the video communication.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: Each individual qualified political advertisement that is distributed or aired to the public in violation of Section 59(1) constitutes a separate violation subject to its own civil fine.
rule_text_technical: Each qualified political advertisement that is distributed or aired to the public that violates this section is a separate violation under subsection (2).

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You are exempt from the AI disclosure requirement if the qualified political advertisement constitutes satire or parody.
rule_text_technical: This section does not apply to a qualified political advertisement that constitutes satire or parody.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You are exempt from the AI disclosure requirement if you are a business or its affiliate regulated by the Michigan Public Service Commission or the Federal Communications Commission.
rule_text_technical: This section does not apply to a business or its affiliate if the business or its affiliate is regulated by the Michigan public service commission or the Federal Communications Commission.

first_instance.law_name: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections) (Michigan, 2023-11-15).

rule_text: You must have competent and reliable evidence to substantiate any claims about the performance, accuracy, or capabilities of your AI systems before making such claims to consumers.
rule_text_technical: Businesses must possess competent and reliable evidence to support material representations about the performance, accuracy, or capabilities of AI systems; unsubstantiated claims regarding accuracy, objectivity, or superiority over human performance constitute deceptive practices under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You cannot use AI-generated content such as reviews, endorsements, or social media posts that creates a false impression of authenticity.
rule_text_technical: AI-generated content including reviews, endorsements, and social media posts that creates a false impression of authenticity or human origin constitutes a deceptive practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You cannot conceal or fail to disclose the use of AI where it makes or substantially influences decisions that materially affect consumers.
rule_text_technical: Where AI is used to make or substantially influence decisions that materially affect consumers, concealment or non-disclosure of AI involvement may constitute a deceptive practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You cannot use AI to infer sensitive characteristics such as race, religion, political affiliation, health status, or sexual orientation from biometric data without meaningful consumer notice and consent.
rule_text_technical: Using AI to infer sensitive characteristics including race, religion, political affiliation, health status, and sexual orientation from biometric data without meaningful consumer notice or consent constitutes a potentially unfair practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You cannot avoid liability under the FTC Act by attributing discriminatory outcomes to an AI system that you deploy.
rule_text_technical: Businesses cannot avoid liability under the FTC Act's prohibition on unfair practices by attributing discriminatory consumer outcomes to an AI system they have chosen to deploy; deployer liability attaches regardless of the AI system being the proximate cause of discrimination.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You cannot use AI-driven dynamic pricing that targets consumers based on characteristics associated with vulnerability.
rule_text_technical: AI-driven price discrimination or dynamic pricing that targets consumers based on characteristics associated with vulnerability constitutes a potentially unfair practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You cannot use AI to infer sensitive personal information from non-sensitive data and then use those inferences to target or harm consumers.
rule_text_technical: Using AI to infer sensitive personal information from non-sensitive data and subsequently using those inferences to target or harm consumers constitutes a potentially unfair practice under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You must implement dispute resolution procedures adequate to address AI-specific error modes in consumer assessments.
rule_text_technical: Consumer reporting agencies using AI to generate consumer assessments must implement dispute resolution procedures that are adequate to address error modes specific to AI systems, as required by FCRA Section 607's mandate to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

rule_text: You must not make misleading claims about how your AI systems work or what data they use.
rule_text_technical: Misleading representations about the functioning of AI systems or the data used in their operation constitute deceptive practices under Section 5 of the FTC Act, subject to FTC enforcement action.

first_instance.law_name: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making

instances.notes: Rule introduced in FTC AI Policy Statement (2023) (FTC, 2023-11-21).

Both require public disclosure of how AI systems work; Peru mandates plain-language descriptions on official websites as a binding legal obligation, while the FTC policy focuses on not making misleading claims about AI systems.

rule_text: You must conduct data trading through a provincially authorized data exchange platform to ensure compliant trading of data products and data services.
rule_text_technical: The Province shall establish or support a provincially authorized data exchange platform for the compliant trading of data products and data services.

first_instance.law_name: Guangdong Province Artificial Intelligence Industry Development Regulations

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Guangdong AI Industry Development Regulations (Guangdong, 2024-03-01).

rule_text: Medical AI applications must comply with applicable medical device regulations and clinical validation requirements before market deployment.
rule_text_technical: Medical AI applications shall comply with applicable medical device regulations and clinical validation requirements; the Province shall establish coordination mechanisms between health authorities and regulatory authorities to facilitate the market access of compliant medical AI products.

first_instance.law_name: Guangdong Province Artificial Intelligence Industry Development Regulations

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Guangdong AI Industry Development Regulations (Guangdong, 2024-03-01).

instances.citation: FDA Thailand / MOH (medical AI devices — Class II)
instances.notes: Both require medical AI applications to comply with medical device regulations and registration before deployment, but Thailand's rule specifically classifies Class II devices and requires pre-market review by Thai FDA.

rule_text: AI applications in the financial sector must be deployed subject to applicable financial regulatory requirements.
rule_text_technical: The Province shall promote AI applications in the financial sector subject to applicable financial regulatory requirements, including AI-enhanced risk management, anti-money laundering, fraud detection, investment advisory, and regulatory technology applications.

first_instance.law_name: Guangdong Province Artificial Intelligence Industry Development Regulations

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Guangdong AI Industry Development Regulations (Guangdong, 2024-03-01).

rule_text: The Province must establish an AI incident monitoring and reporting mechanism.
rule_text_technical: The Province shall establish an AI incident monitoring and reporting mechanism as part of implementing AI governance measures consistent with national requirements.

first_instance.law_name: Guangdong Province Artificial Intelligence Industry Development Regulations

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Guangdong AI Industry Development Regulations (Guangdong, 2024-03-01).

rule_text: You must conduct regular post-deployment monitoring and evaluation of AI system performance and fairness for high-stakes AI applications.
rule_text_technical: Enterprises developing AI applications for high-stakes use cases shall conduct regular post-deployment monitoring and evaluation of AI system performance and fairness.

first_instance.law_name: Guangdong Province Artificial Intelligence Industry Development Regulations

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Guangdong AI Industry Development Regulations (Guangdong, 2024-03-01).

Both require post-deployment monitoring of high-risk AI system performance; Guangdong focuses on performance and fairness monitoring while Peru requires collecting performance data and identifying issues post-market.

rule_text: Developed countries and international organizations should provide technical assistance, training, and institutional capacity building to developing countries to enable them to develop their own AI strategies and regulatory capabilities.
rule_text_technical: It is recommended that developed countries and international organizations provide technical assistance, training, and institutional capacity-building support to developing countries to enable development of national AI strategies and regulatory capabilities.

first_instance.law_name: UN General Assembly Resolution A/78/265: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UN General Assembly AI Resolution (2024) (United Nations, 2024-03-21).

rule_text: Organizations should, on mutually agreed terms, encourage technology transfer and knowledge sharing to help developing countries participate in the global AI ecosystem as developers and innovators, not merely consumers.
rule_text_technical: On mutually agreed terms, it is recommended that technology transfer and knowledge sharing be encouraged to enable developing countries to participate in the global AI ecosystem as developers and innovators.

rule_text: You cannot process personal data scraped from publicly accessible internet sources to train AI models unless data subjects have given explicit consent, the processing falls within a narrowly construed academic research exception with ethics board approval and no commercial AI application, or the data is genuinely public official government information not concerning private individuals.

rule_text: You cannot seriously invade an individual's privacy in a manner that a reasonable person would find highly offensive, and doing so constitutes an actionable tort under Australian law.

rule_text: You are entitled to a statutory safe harbor from liability under this Act for failure-to-disclose and related consumer protection claims if you provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure and have not used AI in a manner that independently violates applicable professional standards.
rule_text_technical: A regulated person who provides a clear and conspicuous disclosure pursuant to Section 1 is entitled to a statutory safe harbor from liability under the Act for: (1) alleged failures to disclose AI use where the disclosure satisfies the clear and conspicuous standard; and (2) consumer protection claims arising from AI use where the regulated person has complied with disclosure requirements and has not used AI in a manner that independently violates applicable professional standards.

rule_text: Individuals have the right to ask any regulated person whether AI is being used in their interaction, what the AI's role is, and whether a human professional reviewed AI-generated outputs before they were communicated to the consumer.
rule_text_technical: SB 226 codifies the right of any consumer, in any interaction with a regulated person, to inquire: (1) whether AI is being used in the interaction; (2) what the AI's role is; and (3) whether a human professional reviewed AI-generated outputs before they were communicated to the consumer.

rule_text: If you are a licensed physician, nurse, attorney, financial adviser, insurance agent, mortgage loan originator, real estate agent or broker, mental health professional, or licensed educator, you are expressly subject to the AI disclosure requirements of this Act.
rule_text_technical: The following licensed professions are expressly covered by the AI disclosure requirements of Utah Code § 13-2-8 as amended by SB 226: licensed physicians, nurses, and healthcare providers under Utah Code Title 58; licensed attorneys and legal service providers; licensed financial advisers, insurance agents, and mortgage loan originators; licensed real estate agents and brokers; licensed mental health professionals including counselors, social workers, and marriage and family therapists; and licensed educators in regulated educational settings.

rule_text: You must label AI-generated content in accordance with these Measures and GB 45438-2025, and you bear primary responsibility for ensuring all AI-generated content made available to users is properly labelled.
rule_text_technical: Service providers shall label AI-generated content in accordance with these Measures and the relevant requirements of mandatory national standard GB 45438-2025, and bear the primary responsibility for ensuring that AI-generated content they make available to users is properly labelled.

rule_text: You must place a clear label at the beginning or end of any short-form AI-generated text of one hundred Chinese characters or fewer.
rule_text_technical: Short-form text of one hundred Chinese characters or fewer that is entirely AI-generated shall bear a clear label at the beginning or end of the text.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

rule_text: You must place a label at the beginning of any long-form text that is substantially AI-generated, and may additionally include section-level labels where appropriate.
rule_text_technical: Long-form text that is substantially AI-generated shall bear a label at the beginning, and may additionally include section-level labels where appropriate.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

rule_text: You must label AI-assisted editing that materially alters the meaning or factual content of original human-authored text.
rule_text_technical: AI-assisted editing that materially alters the meaning or factual content of original human-authored text shall also require labelling.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

rule_text: You must attach individual labels to each AI-generated image when such images are embedded in articles, web pages, or multimedia content.
rule_text_technical: Where AI-generated images are embedded in articles, web pages, or multimedia content, labels shall be attached to each individual image.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

rule_text: You must apply enhanced labelling and disclosure requirements where AI-generated voice closely resembles or is intended to mimic the voice of a specific real person.
rule_text_technical: Where the AI-generated voice closely resembles or is intended to mimic the voice of a specific real person, enhanced labelling and disclosure requirements apply.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

rule_text: You must include a prominent label in the title, description, or introductory segment of AI-generated or AI-altered video content.
rule_text_technical: AI-generated or significantly altered video content shall bear a prominent label in the title, description, or introductory segment of the video.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Both require prominent visible labels (not merely metadata) on AI-generated video/synthetic media, but this rule extends to all synthetic media types and mandates on-screen visibility, while the Chinese rule focuses on video titles and descriptions.

rule_text: You must establish automated detection mechanisms to identify unlabelled AI-generated content uploaded by users and prompt those users to add appropriate labels.
rule_text_technical: Online information content platforms shall establish mechanisms to detect AI-generated content uploaded by users using automated content detection tools and prompt users who appear to have uploaded unlabelled AI-generated content to add appropriate labels.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

instances.citation: Mandatory Labeling Obligations for SSMIs — AI Content Labeling Requirement (¶1)
instances.notes: Both require platforms to implement automated detection mechanisms to identify unlabelled AI-generated content uploaded by users, but the Indian rule is binding on SSMIs and includes technical specifics, while the Chinese rule is also binding but in a different regulatory context with different scope.

rule_text: You must provide users with convenient tools to add AI-generated content labels when uploading content to your platform.
rule_text_technical: Platforms shall provide users with convenient tools to add AI-generated content labels when uploading content.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

instances.citation: Mandatory Labeling Obligations for SSMIs — User Disclosure at Upload
instances.notes: Both require platforms to provide mechanisms for users to declare AI-generated status at upload, but this rule goes further by requiring terms of service updates and mandatory declarations at the upload interface, while the Chinese rule merely provides convenient labeling tools.

rule_text: You cannot allow users to remove, conceal, or deliberately obscure AI-generated content labels, and must implement technical safeguards to prevent unauthorized removal of such labels.
rule_text_technical: Platforms shall not allow users to remove, conceal, or deliberately obscure labels that have been applied to AI-generated content by service providers or that are required under these Measures, and shall implement technical safeguards to prevent the unauthorized removal of AI-generated content labels.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China AI Labelling Measures (GB45438-2025) (China, 2025-03-14).

instances.citation: Mandatory Labeling Obligations for SSMIs — Synthetic Media Enhanced Labeling (¶2c)
instances.notes: Both prohibit removal or concealment of AI-generated content labels, but this rule additionally requires labels to persist when content is downloaded or screenshotted, addressing a technical gap not covered by the Chinese rule.

rule_text: You must apply required labels to AI-generated content before displaying it to users and cannot display AI-generated content to users without the required labels.
rule_text_technical: Platforms that have the capability to generate or recommend AI-generated content shall apply required labels to such content before it is displayed to users, and shall not display AI-generated content to users without the required labels.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

instances.citation: Mandatory Labeling Obligations for SSMIs — AI Content Labeling Requirement (¶2)
instances.notes: Both require mandatory automatic labeling of AI-generated content before display to users, but this rule applies to built-in AI generation tools on platforms, whereas the Chinese rule applies to content display generally.

rule_text: You must maintain records of the labelling status of AI-generated content on your platform, make those records available to regulatory authorities upon request, and submit annual reports on labelling implementation to the relevant regulatory authority.
rule_text_technical: Platforms shall maintain records of the labelling status of AI-generated content distributed on their platforms and make such records available to regulatory authorities upon request. Platforms shall report annually to the relevant regulatory authority on the implementation of AI-generated content labelling requirements.

first_instance.law_name: Measures for Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Synthetic Content; Technical Standard GB45438-2025

rule_text: You cannot assist users in generating or distributing AI-generated content that is deliberately designed to deceive audiences about its AI-generated origin, including content structured to evade content moderation systems.
rule_text_technical: Service providers and platforms shall not assist users in generating or distributing AI-generated content that is deliberately designed to deceive audiences about its AI-generated origin, including AI-generated content that is structured to evade detection by content moderation systems.

rule_text: In law enforcement processing, the safeguard obligations under s. 50C(1) and (2) do not apply if an exemption is required for one of the listed reasons, the controller reconsiders the decision as soon as reasonably practicable, and there is meaningful human involvement in that reconsideration.

rule_text: The exemption from safeguard obligations in law enforcement automated decision-making applies only where it is required to avoid obstructing an inquiry, avoid prejudicing criminal proceedings, protect public security, safeguard national security, or protect the rights and freedoms of others.

instances.notes: Rule introduced in South Africa POPIA (South Africa, 2013-11-26).

rule_text: You must submit a formal application for registration as a data controller or data processor in the prescribed manner.
rule_text_technical: An application for registration as a data controller or data processor must be made in accordance with the prescribed procedure under section 19 of the Act.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: Your registration certificate as a data controller or data processor may be cancelled or varied by the Data Commissioner under prescribed conditions.
rule_text_technical: The Data Commissioner has the power to cancel or vary a registration certificate issued to a data controller or data processor in accordance with section 22.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: You must have a mechanism enabling data subjects to exercise their rights under this Act.
rule_text_technical: Data controllers must facilitate the exercise of rights by data subjects in accordance with the procedures set out in section 27.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: You must comply with the specific rules applicable to further categories of sensitive personal data as designated under this section.
rule_text_technical: Section 47 establishes further categories of sensitive personal data and the applicable processing conditions and restrictions for such categories.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: The Data Commissioner may grant exemptions from certain provisions of this Act in prescribed circumstances.
rule_text_technical: Under section 54, the Data Commissioner is empowered to grant exemptions from specified requirements of the Act in circumstances determined to warrant such exemptions.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: You must comply with any data-sharing code issued under this Act when sharing personal data.
rule_text_technical: Section 55 provides for the establishment of a data-sharing code, compliance with which is required when data controllers or processors share personal data.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: You must comply with a preservation order issued by the Data Commissioner requiring the preservation of personal data.
rule_text_technical: The Data Commissioner is empowered under section 66 to issue preservation orders requiring data controllers or processors to preserve specified personal data, with which compliance is mandatory.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: The Data Commissioner and staff of the Office are protected from personal liability for acts done in good faith in the exercise of their functions under this Act.
rule_text_technical: Section 17 provides that the Data Commissioner and staff of the Office shall not be personally liable for any act or omission done in good faith in the performance of their functions or duties under the Act.

first_instance.law_name: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (Kenya, 2019-11-08).

rule_text: You must handle personal information in a way that recognises both the right of individuals to have their privacy protected and the need for information to flow freely for legitimate purposes.
rule_text_technical: The purpose of this Act is to promote and protect individual privacy in general and, in particular, to— (a) provide a framework for the protection of individual privacy; and (b) promote and protect individual privacy by establishing information privacy principles that agencies must comply with.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must comply with this Act if you are an agency operating in New Zealand or if you collect, use, or disclose personal information about New Zealand individuals.
rule_text_technical: This Act applies to agencies in respect of personal information they hold, collect, use, or disclose, subject to specified exceptions and limitations set out in the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Privacy Commissioner must perform the statutory functions assigned under this Act, including oversight of agency compliance with information privacy principles.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner has the functions specified in this Act, including promoting and protecting individual privacy, monitoring compliance with the Act, and investigating complaints about interference with privacy of individuals.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Privacy Commissioner must act independently when carrying out statutory functions and is not subject to ministerial direction in the exercise of those functions.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner must act independently in the performance of the Commissioner's functions and the exercise of the Commissioner's powers under this Act.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Individuals have the right to access personal information that an agency holds about them.
rule_text_technical: Information Privacy Principle 6: Where an agency holds personal information in such a way that it can readily be retrieved, the individual concerned must be able to obtain from the agency confirmation of whether or not the agency holds such personal information, and, if the agency holds such personal information, access to that information.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not disclose personal information to a third party unless the disclosure is for the purpose for which it was collected or an applicable exception applies.
rule_text_technical: Information Privacy Principle 11: An agency that holds personal information must not disclose the information to a person or body or agency unless the agency believes on reasonable grounds that— (a) the disclosure is one of the purposes in connection with which the information was obtained or is directly related to the purposes in connection with which the information was obtained; or (b) the source of the information is a publicly available publication; or (c) the disclosure is authorised by the individual concerned; or (d) non-compliance is necessary for specified reasons including law enforcement, legal proceedings, health and safety, or the public interest.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not assign a unique identifier to an individual if it is the same identifier used by another agency, unless specifically authorised; and you must not require someone to provide a unique identifier unless that identifier relates to the purpose for which it is required.
rule_text_technical: Information Privacy Principle 13: An agency must not assign a unique identifier to an individual unless the assignment is necessary to enable the agency to carry out its functions efficiently; must not assign to an individual a unique identifier that has been assigned by another agency except in specified circumstances; and must not require an individual to provide their unique identifier except when the requirement relates to the purpose for which it was assigned.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If your agency holds personal information overseas, the information privacy principles still apply to that information as if it were held in New Zealand.
rule_text_technical: The information privacy principles apply in relation to personal information held by an agency outside New Zealand in the same way as they apply to personal information held in New Zealand.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may authorise collection, use, storage, or disclosure of personal information that would otherwise breach IPP 2 or IPPs 9 to 12, subject to conditions the Commissioner may impose.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may, on application by an agency or on the Commissioner's own initiative, authorise the collection, use, storage, or disclosure of personal information that would otherwise be in breach of IPP 2 or IPPs 9 to 12, subject to any conditions the Commissioner thinks fit.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Breaches of the information privacy principles are enforceable through the complaint and proceedings mechanisms set out in this Act.
rule_text_technical: A breach of an information privacy principle is not of itself an offence; however, it may be the subject of a complaint and may result in proceedings before the Human Rights Review Tribunal, which may grant remedies including damages.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may issue codes of practice that modify how one or more information privacy principles apply to specified agencies, activities, or personal information.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may issue codes of practice that apply instead of or in addition to specified information privacy principles in relation to specified agencies, activities, or personal information, after following the required consultation process.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Where a code of practice applies, you must comply with the code instead of or in addition to the relevant information privacy principles as specified in the code.
rule_text_technical: Where a code of practice applies, the code has effect as if it were part of this Act and the relevant information privacy principles apply subject to the code.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Individuals may request urgency in processing an IPP 6 access request, and agencies must treat the request with urgency if the request is urgent.
rule_text_technical: An individual making an IPP 6 request may indicate that the request is urgent, and an agency that receives an urgent IPP 6 request must treat the request with urgency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must take reasonable steps to assist an individual who wants to make an IPP 6 request to do so, including identifying the information sought.
rule_text_technical: An agency must take reasonable steps to assist an individual who wishes to make an IPP 6 request and is having difficulty formulating the request, including by advising the individual about what information may be available.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If an IPP 6 request is made to the wrong agency, you must transfer the request to the appropriate agency and notify the individual, or notify the individual of the correct agency to contact.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency receives an IPP 6 request and the agency does not hold the information or the request would more properly be dealt with by another agency, the agency must transfer the request to that other agency and notify the individual, or notify the individual of the appropriate agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you decide to grant an IPP 6 access request, you must provide access to the personal information in the manner requested by the individual or in such other manner as is reasonable in the circumstances.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency grants an IPP 6 request, it must give the individual access to the personal information in the manner requested by the individual, or if that is not reasonably practicable, in such other manner as is reasonable in the circumstances.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may refuse an IPP 6 access request only on grounds specified in the Act, and you must notify the individual of the refusal and the grounds for it.
rule_text_technical: An agency may refuse an IPP 6 request only on the grounds specified in sections 49–53 of this Act and must notify the individual of the refusal, the grounds on which it is refused, and the individual's right to complain to the Commissioner.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: In certain circumstances, you may respond to an IPP 6 request by neither confirming nor denying that personal information is held — but only where confirming or denying would itself be grounds for refusal.
rule_text_technical: An agency may respond to an IPP 6 request by neither confirming nor denying whether it holds personal information about the individual, where to do otherwise would itself constitute a ground for refusing access to the information under sections 49–53.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may extend the 20-working-day time limit for responding to an IPP 6 request in specified circumstances, but you must notify the individual of the extension and the reason for it.
rule_text_technical: An agency may extend the time limit for responding to an IPP 6 request where the request is for a large amount of information, or where meeting the time limit would unreasonably interfere with operations of the agency, but must notify the individual of the extension and the new time limit.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may refuse access to personal information if granting access would be likely to endanger the safety of any individual.
rule_text_technical: An agency may refuse access to personal information where the agency is satisfied that the withholding of the information is necessary to prevent a serious threat to the life or health of the individual who made the request, or to another individual.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may refuse access to personal information that comprises evaluative material, where that material was supplied under conditions of confidentiality.
rule_text_technical: An agency may refuse to disclose personal information that consists of evaluative material compiled solely for the purpose of determining suitability, eligibility, or qualifications, where the information was supplied by the person who compiled it in the expectation that it would be held in confidence.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may refuse access to personal information where disclosure would be likely to prejudice the security, defence, or international relations of New Zealand.
rule_text_technical: An agency may refuse access to personal information where the agency is satisfied that the withholding of the information is necessary to avoid prejudice to the security or defence of New Zealand or the international relations of the Government of New Zealand.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may refuse access to personal information that constitutes a trade secret or whose disclosure would unreasonably prejudice the commercial position of the agency.
rule_text_technical: An agency may refuse access to personal information if to do so would disclose a trade secret or would be likely unreasonably to prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied the information or the subject of the information.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may refuse access to personal information on other statutory grounds, including where disclosure would constitute a contempt of court, or where the information relates to another individual whose privacy would be prejudiced.
rule_text_technical: An agency may refuse access to personal information on additional grounds specified in section 53, including where disclosure would constitute contempt of court, would be contrary to another enactment, or would involve the unwarranted disclosure of the affairs of another individual.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Instead of refusing access to personal information outright, you may impose conditions on how the individual may access the information.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency would be entitled to refuse access to personal information, the agency may instead impose conditions on the granting of access to the information, including conditions relating to the way in which the individual may use the information.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may withhold only the parts of a document that are protected from disclosure, and must provide access to the remaining parts of the document.
rule_text_technical: Where a document contains personal information to which access must be refused, the agency must withhold only that information and must, where it is reasonably practicable, provide access to the remainder of the document.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must make personal information available in the format requested by the individual where reasonably practicable, which may include allowing inspection or providing a copy.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency grants access to personal information contained in a document, the access may be provided by allowing inspection of the document, providing a copy, or any other means agreed between the agency and the individual.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Before providing access to personal information, you must take reasonable steps to verify the identity of the person requesting access.
rule_text_technical: Before giving access to personal information, an agency must take reasonable steps to verify that the individual requesting access is the individual to whom the information relates, or is authorised to act on behalf of that individual.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Individuals may request urgency in processing a correction request, and agencies must treat the request as urgent where urgency is requested.
rule_text_technical: An individual making a correction request may indicate that the request is urgent, and an agency that receives an urgent correction request must treat it with urgency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must take reasonable steps to assist an individual who is having difficulty formulating a correction request.
rule_text_technical: An agency must take reasonable steps to assist an individual who wishes to make a correction request and is having difficulty formulating the request.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If a correction request is made to the wrong agency, you must transfer it to the appropriate agency or notify the individual of the correct agency.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency receives a correction request and the information is not held by the agency or would more properly be dealt with by another agency, the agency must transfer the request to that other agency and notify the individual, or notify the individual of the appropriate agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may extend the 20-working-day time limit for responding to a correction request in specified circumstances, but you must notify the individual of the extension.
rule_text_technical: An agency may extend the time limit for responding to a correction request in specified circumstances and must notify the individual of the extension and the reason for it.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Private sector agencies may charge individuals for responding to an IPP 6 access request, but only in accordance with regulations and any applicable guidelines issued by the Commissioner.
rule_text_technical: An agency may charge an individual for the cost of making personal information available in response to an IPP 6 request, but only in accordance with the regulations and subject to any guidelines issued by the Commissioner.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may authorise a public sector agency to impose charges for responding to IPP 6 requests, subject to conditions.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may, on application, authorise a public sector agency to impose a charge for making personal information available in response to an IPP 6 request, subject to any conditions the Commissioner specifies.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: An interference with the privacy of an individual occurs when an agency breaches an information privacy principle and causes harm to the individual, or in other specified circumstances.
rule_text_technical: An action of an agency is an interference with the privacy of an individual if— (a) the action breaches an information privacy principle and the action causes, or may cause, loss, detriment, damage, or injury to the individual; or (b) the action is a breach of an information privacy principle that was intentional or reckless; or other specified circumstances.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: A complaint may be made by the individual whose privacy has been interfered with, or by another person or body on that individual's behalf.
rule_text_technical: A complaint to the Commissioner may be made by— (a) the individual whose privacy has been interfered with; (b) a person duly authorised to act on behalf of that individual; or (c) in certain circumstances, a body or organisation acting on behalf of a class of individuals.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: When the Commissioner receives a complaint, the Commissioner must decide whether to investigate it and notify the complainant of the decision.
rule_text_technical: On receipt of a complaint, the Commissioner must decide whether to investigate the complaint and must notify the complainant of the Commissioner's decision, giving reasons if the Commissioner decides not to investigate.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may decide not to investigate a complaint in specified circumstances, including where the complaint is frivolous, vexatious, or not made in good faith.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may decide not to investigate a complaint, or not to continue an investigation, where the Commissioner is satisfied that— (a) the complaint is frivolous, vexatious, or not made in good faith; (b) the individual has not suffered adequate harm; (c) the subject matter of the complaint is trivial; or (d) other specified circumstances apply.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may refer a complaint to another person or body that has the ability to deal with the complaint more appropriately.
rule_text_technical: Where the Commissioner considers that a complaint could be more appropriately dealt with by another person or body, the Commissioner may refer the complaint to that person or body and notify the complainant of the referral.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may refer a complaint to an overseas privacy enforcement authority if the complaint relates to actions of an overseas agency.
rule_text_technical: Where a complaint relates to the actions of an overseas agency, the Commissioner may refer the complaint to an overseas privacy enforcement authority and notify the complainant of the referral.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)
