instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may, without conducting a formal investigation, explore the possibility of settling the complaint or obtaining an assurance from the agency about future conduct.
rule_text_technical: Before commencing an investigation, the Commissioner may explore the possibility of a settlement being reached between the parties to the complaint or obtaining from the agency an assurance about future conduct relating to the subject matter of the complaint.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may refer a complaint to the Director of Human Rights Proceedings without conducting an investigation, where the Commissioner considers that appropriate.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may, without conducting an investigation, refer a complaint to the Director of Human Rights Proceedings if the Commissioner considers that such a referral is appropriate in the circumstances.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: When conducting an investigation, the Commissioner must observe the rules of natural justice and may conduct the investigation in the manner the Commissioner thinks fit.
rule_text_technical: In conducting an investigation, the Commissioner must observe the rules of natural justice and, subject to that requirement, may conduct the investigation in such a manner as the Commissioner thinks fit.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may require the parties to a complaint to attend a compulsory conference to attempt to resolve the complaint.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may, at any stage of the investigation of a complaint, require the parties to the complaint to attend a conference presided over by the Commissioner or a person nominated by the Commissioner.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may summon any person to appear before the Commissioner to provide information or documents relevant to an investigation.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of an investigation, the Commissioner may, by notice in writing, require any person to appear before the Commissioner at a time and place specified in the notice to provide information or to produce documents.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must disclose information to the Commissioner when required, even if you would otherwise be bound by an obligation of secrecy or confidentiality.
rule_text_technical: A person is not excused from providing information or producing documents to the Commissioner for the purposes of an investigation on the ground that doing so would breach an obligation of secrecy or confidentiality imposed by any enactment or rule of law.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Individuals required to provide information during an investigation have the same protections and privileges as witnesses in court proceedings.
rule_text_technical: A person required to provide information or produce documents during an investigation by the Commissioner has the same privileges and protections as a witness in a court of law.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Information disclosed to the Commissioner during an investigation is privileged and cannot be used against the person who provided it in any other proceedings.
rule_text_technical: No information disclosed to the Commissioner in the course of an investigation, and no document produced to the Commissioner in the course of an investigation, is admissible as evidence in any proceedings other than proceedings for perjury or an offence under this Act.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If an investigation finds that access to personal information was wrongly refused, the Commissioner may issue an access direction requiring the agency to provide access.
rule_text_technical: Following an investigation relating to access to personal information, the Commissioner may issue an access direction requiring an agency to provide access to personal information where the Commissioner finds that access was wrongly refused.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: After completing an investigation that is not about access to personal information, the Commissioner must report findings to the relevant parties and may make recommendations about remedying the breach.
rule_text_technical: After completing an investigation other than one relating to access to personal information or charging, the Commissioner must report the findings to the complainant and the agency, and may recommend that the agency take specified action to remedy the interference with privacy.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner must report to the appropriate authority if an investigation reveals a breach of duty or misconduct by an officer or employee of an agency.
rule_text_technical: If in the course of an investigation the Commissioner is of the opinion that there has been a breach of duty or misconduct by any officer, employee, or member of an agency, the Commissioner must inform the appropriate authority.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Director of Human Rights Proceedings may commence proceedings before the Human Rights Review Tribunal in respect of a complaint about an interference with privacy.
rule_text_technical: The Director of Human Rights Proceedings may, with the consent of the complainant, bring proceedings before the Human Rights Review Tribunal in respect of any matter referred to the Director by the Commissioner under this Act.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: In proceedings before the Human Rights Review Tribunal for interference with privacy, the agency bears the burden of proving that its actions were justified.
rule_text_technical: In proceedings before the Tribunal, the onus of proof lies on the defendant agency to establish that any interference with the privacy of the individual was justified.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Human Rights Review Tribunal may grant remedies for interference with privacy, including damages, declarations, and orders requiring the agency to remedy the interference.
rule_text_technical: Where the Tribunal finds that there has been an interference with the privacy of an individual, the Tribunal may grant one or more of the following remedies: a declaration that the action of the defendant was an interference with the privacy of the plaintiff; an order requiring the defendant to remedy the interference; damages; an order restraining the defendant from continuing or repeating the interference; or other specified remedies.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Human Rights Review Tribunal may award damages to an individual for interference with their privacy, including compensation for loss, humiliation, and injury to feelings.
rule_text_technical: The Tribunal may award damages against a defendant for interference with the privacy of an individual, including damages for pecuniary loss, loss of benefit, humiliation, loss of dignity, and injury to the feelings of the individual.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: An agency that fails to comply with an access direction issued by the Commissioner may be ordered by the Human Rights Review Tribunal to comply.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency fails to comply with an access direction, the Director of Human Rights Proceedings or the aggrieved individual may apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring the agency to comply with the access direction.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: An agency may appeal to the Human Rights Review Tribunal against an access direction issued by the Commissioner.
rule_text_technical: A defendant who is aggrieved by an access direction issued by the Commissioner may appeal to the Tribunal against the direction.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must assess the likelihood that a privacy breach will cause serious harm by considering specified factors including the sensitivity of the information and the nature of the harm likely to result.
rule_text_technical: In assessing whether a privacy breach is reasonably likely to cause serious harm, an agency must take into account specified factors, including the sensitivity of the information, the nature of the harm that could result, the number of individuals affected, the security measures in place, and the identity of the person who obtained the information.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may delay or be exempt from the requirement to notify affected individuals of a notifiable privacy breach in specified circumstances, such as where notification would prejudice a law enforcement investigation.
rule_text_technical: An agency is not required to notify affected individuals or give public notice of a notifiable privacy breach in specified circumstances, including where notification would prejudice the maintenance of the law, the life or health of any individual, or where the Commissioner exempts the agency from notification.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Any notification of a notifiable privacy breach to affected individuals must include specified information, including a description of the breach, the type of information affected, and what steps can be taken to mitigate harm.
rule_text_technical: A notification of a notifiable privacy breach to affected individuals or by public notice must contain— (a) a description of the breach; (b) the type of personal information concerned; (c) what steps the agency has taken or intends to take to address the breach; (d) what steps affected individuals can take to reduce the risk of harm; and (e) the contact details of the agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: An agency is liable for the actions of its officers, employees, and agents relating to privacy breaches as if those actions were the agency's own, unless the agency took reasonable precautions to prevent those actions.
rule_text_technical: An agency is liable for any act or omission of its officers, employees, agents, or members that constitutes an offence under sections 118 or 211 as if the act or omission were done or omitted by the agency, unless the agency took reasonable precautions and exercised due diligence to avoid the act or omission.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Knowledge of a privacy breach by an officer, employee, agent, or member of an agency is to be treated as knowledge of the agency for the purposes of the breach notification obligations.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of the notifiable privacy breach provisions, knowledge that a notifiable privacy breach has occurred that is acquired by an officer, employee, agent, or member of an agency in the course of their duties is to be treated as knowledge of the agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may publish the identity of agencies that have been found to have committed offences relating to failure to notify a notifiable privacy breach.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency has been convicted of an offence under section 118 or section 211, or where an agency has repeatedly failed to comply with the notifiable privacy breach notification requirements, the Commissioner may publish the identity of the agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Before issuing a compliance notice, the Commissioner must give the agency an opportunity to be heard and must consider the agency's response.
rule_text_technical: Before issuing a compliance notice, the Commissioner must give the agency an opportunity to make submissions and must consider any submissions made before deciding whether to issue the notice.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: A compliance notice must be in writing and must specify the actions required, the time within which they must be taken, and the right to appeal.
rule_text_technical: A compliance notice must be in writing and must specify— (a) the action or inaction that constitutes or may constitute a contravention; (b) the action required to be taken or refrained from; (c) the time within which the required action must be taken; and (d) the right of the agency to appeal against the notice.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may vary or cancel a compliance notice if the circumstances change or if the agency demonstrates compliance.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may vary or cancel a compliance notice at any time by notice in writing to the agency, including where the agency has taken or agreed to take the required action.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may require agencies to provide information to enable the Commissioner to assess compliance with a compliance notice.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of monitoring compliance with a compliance notice, the Commissioner may require an agency to provide information to the Commissioner within a specified time.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Commissioner may publish details of compliance notices issued to agencies, including the agency's identity and the actions required.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may, if satisfied it is in the public interest to do so, publish details of a compliance notice, including the identity of the agency and the nature of the contravention or likely contravention.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If an agency fails to comply with a compliance notice, the Director of Human Rights Proceedings or the Commissioner may apply to the Human Rights Review Tribunal for an order requiring compliance.
rule_text_technical: Where an agency fails to comply with a compliance notice, the Director of Human Rights Proceedings or the Commissioner may apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring the agency to comply with the notice.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: The Human Rights Review Tribunal may make an interim order suspending a compliance notice pending the determination of an appeal.
rule_text_technical: On an appeal against a compliance notice, the Tribunal may make an interim order suspending the operation of the compliance notice until the appeal is determined.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must design and manufacture connected products and related services so that product data is accessible to users by default, easily, securely, free of charge, in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
rule_text_technical: Connected products shall be designed and manufactured, and related services shall be designed and provided, such that product data is, by default, easily, securely, and free of charge directly accessible to the user in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, where technically feasible.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Before concluding a purchase contract, you must disclose to users the type and format of data the product can generate, whether data is stored on-device or remotely, retention periods, and methods of access and erasure.
rule_text_technical: Prior to the conclusion of a purchase contract, sellers of connected products must disclose: the type and format of data the product can generate, whether the data is stored on-device or remotely, applicable retention periods, and the methods by which the user may access or erase such data.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You must make data readily available to users without undue delay, in machine-readable format, and free of charge.
rule_text_technical: Data holders are obliged to make data readily available to users without undue delay, in a machine-readable format, and free of charge to the user.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot make data access unduly difficult through non-neutral means.
rule_text_technical: Data holders are prohibited from making access to data unduly difficult through the use of non-neutral technical or other means.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot retain unnecessary access logs relating to users' data access activities.
rule_text_technical: Data holders are prohibited from retaining access logs that are not necessary in connection with the data access activities of users.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Where data access involves trade secrets, you must implement proportionate technical and organisational measures and may require confidentiality agreements before disclosure.
rule_text_technical: Where the making available of data requires disclosure of trade secrets, the data holder must apply proportionate technical and organisational measures to preserve confidentiality, and may require the conclusion of a confidentiality agreement prior to disclosure.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You may suspend data sharing if the user or third party fails to implement required confidentiality measures for trade secrets.
rule_text_technical: Data holders may suspend the making available of data where the user or third party fails to implement the technical and organisational measures required to protect confidentiality of trade secrets.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: In exceptional circumstances, you may refuse data access if you can demonstrate that sharing is likely to cause serious economic damage.
rule_text_technical: In exceptional circumstances, a data holder may refuse to make data available where it can demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the competent authority, that making data available is likely to cause serious economic damage to the data holder or third parties.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Gatekeepers designated under the Digital Markets Act cannot be eligible third parties to receive data under this provision.
rule_text_technical: Legal or natural persons designated as gatekeepers pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 (Digital Markets Act) are not eligible as third parties for the purposes of receiving data under Article 5.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Third parties cannot use coercive means to access data or use data to derive competitive insights about the data holder.
rule_text_technical: Third parties are prohibited from using coercive means to obtain access to data and from using received data to derive competitive intelligence concerning the data holder.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you must use the data only for the purposes and conditions agreed with the user.
rule_text_technical: Third parties receiving data under Article 5 must use the data exclusively for the purposes and under the conditions agreed with the user at the time of the data access request.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you cannot profile users except where strictly necessary for the agreed service.
rule_text_technical: Third parties receiving data under Article 5 are prohibited from profiling individuals within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, except where such profiling is strictly necessary to provide the service requested by the user.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you cannot share the data with other third parties unless contractually authorised to do so.
rule_text_technical: Third parties receiving data under Article 5 are prohibited from making such data available to other third parties unless explicitly authorised to do so under the contractual terms agreed with the user.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you cannot make data available to gatekeepers.
rule_text_technical: Third parties receiving data under Article 5 are prohibited from making such data available to persons designated as gatekeepers pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2022/1925.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you cannot use the data to develop competing products against the data holder.
rule_text_technical: Third parties receiving data under Article 5 are prohibited from using such data to develop a product or service that competes with the connected product or related service from which the data originates.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you cannot ignore agreed confidentiality measures for trade secrets.
rule_text_technical: Third parties receiving data under Article 5 must comply with any technical and organisational measures agreed with the data holder for the preservation of trade secret confidentiality.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Chapter II obligations do not apply to data generated by microenterprises or small enterprises, unless they are acting as subcontractors.
rule_text_technical: The obligations set out in Chapter II of the Data Act do not apply to data generated by connected products or related services provided by microenterprises or small enterprises as defined in Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC, unless such enterprises act as subcontractors.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Medium-sized enterprises that have recently qualified as such are exempt from Chapter II obligations for one year following that qualification.
rule_text_technical: Medium-sized enterprises that have only recently ceased to qualify as small enterprises within the meaning of Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC are exempt from the obligations of Chapter II for a period of one year from the date on which they ceased to so qualify.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Where you are obliged under Union law to make data available, you must do so under fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory (FRAND) terms in a transparent manner.
rule_text_technical: Where a data holder is obliged under Union law to make data available to data recipients, such data must be made available under fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory terms and conditions and in a transparent manner.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You must treat comparable categories of data recipients uniformly when making data available.
rule_text_technical: Data holders must apply equivalent terms and conditions to data recipients belonging to comparable categories, and must not discriminate between such recipients without objective justification.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Any compensation agreed between data holders and data recipients must be non-discriminatory and reasonable, taking into account the costs of data formatting, dissemination, and investment in collection.
rule_text_technical: Compensation agreed between data holders and data recipients for making data available must be non-discriminatory and reasonable, and its calculation must take into account the costs of data formatting and dissemination as well as investments made in data collection and production.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Where the data recipient is an SME or a not-for-profit research organisation, compensation is capped at the direct costs of making the data available, excluding any return on investment.
rule_text_technical: Where the data recipient is a small or medium-sized enterprise or a not-for-profit research organisation, compensation shall not exceed the direct costs attributable to making the data available and shall not include a return on investment for the data holder.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: The Commission must develop guidelines for calculating reasonable compensation for data access.
rule_text_technical: The European Commission is required to develop non-binding guidelines to assist parties in calculating reasonable compensation for the making available of data under Chapter III.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Users, data holders, and data recipients have the right to access certified dispute settlement bodies to resolve disputes arising from data access obligations.
rule_text_technical: Users, data holders, and data recipients have the right to refer disputes concerning data access and use under this Regulation to certified dispute settlement bodies that are impartial, independent, and possess the necessary expertise.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Dispute settlement bodies must adopt their decisions within 90 days of receiving a request.
rule_text_technical: Certified dispute settlement bodies must adopt decisions within 90 calendar days of receipt of a complete dispute resolution request.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Decisions of dispute settlement bodies are binding only where both parties have explicitly consented to be bound, and judicial remedies are preserved in all cases.
rule_text_technical: Decisions of certified dispute settlement bodies are binding on the parties only where both parties have explicitly consented to such binding effect; the right to pursue judicial remedies is preserved in all circumstances.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You may apply technical protection measures such as smart contracts and encryption to prevent unauthorised data access, provided such measures do not discriminate between recipients or hinder user rights.
rule_text_technical: Data holders may apply technical protection measures, including smart contracts and encryption, to prevent unauthorised access to data, provided that such measures are applied in a non-discriminatory manner and do not impede the exercise of user rights under this Regulation.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Third parties and recipients who misuse data must comply with data holder requests to erase data, cease production of goods derived from unlawfully used data, and provide compensation.
rule_text_technical: Where data has been accessed or used unlawfully, third parties and data recipients must, upon request of the data holder, erase the data, cease the production of goods or services derived from the unlawfully used data, and provide appropriate compensation to the data holder.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term concerning data access, use, liability, or remedies that is unilaterally imposed by one enterprise on another is not binding if it is unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term concerning data access, data use, liability for data, or remedies for breach of data-related obligations, which has been unilaterally imposed by one enterprise upon another, shall not be binding on the disadvantaged party if it is unfair within the meaning of this Article.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term is unfair if it grossly deviates from good commercial practice in data access and use, contrary to good faith and fair dealing.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term is unfair for the purposes of Article 13 where it grossly deviates from good commercial practice in data access and use, contrary to the requirements of good faith and fair dealing.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot include a contractual term that excludes liability for intentional acts or gross negligence.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that excludes liability for intentional misconduct or gross negligence in connection with data access or use is conclusively unfair and shall not be binding on the disadvantaged party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot include a contractual term that eliminates all remedies available to the other party for non-performance.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that eliminates all remedies available to one party in the event of non-performance by the other party is conclusively unfair and shall not be binding on the disadvantaged party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot include a contractual term that grants one party exclusive rights to determine the interpretation of the contract.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term granting one party the exclusive right to determine the meaning or interpretation of contractual provisions is conclusively unfair and shall not be binding on the disadvantaged party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term that inappropriately limits remedies or extends liability beyond what is commercially reasonable is presumed to be unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term is presumptively unfair where it inappropriately limits the remedies available to one party or extends liability beyond what is commercially reasonable in data access and use contexts, unless the imposing party can rebut this presumption.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term that allows detrimental access to commercially sensitive information is presumed to be unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that grants one party access to commercially sensitive information of the other party in a manner that is detrimental to the latter's commercial interests is presumptively unfair, subject to rebuttal.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term that prevents the use of provided data is presumed to be unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that prevents one party from using data that has been provided to it under the contract is presumptively unfair, subject to rebuttal by the imposing party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term that restricts the right to terminate the agreement or prevents the making of data copies is presumed to be unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that disproportionately restricts a party's right to terminate the contract or that prevents a party from making copies of data held under the contract is presumptively unfair, subject to rebuttal.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term enabling unreasonably short termination notice periods is presumed to be unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that enables one party to give unreasonably short notice of termination of a data access or use agreement is presumptively unfair, subject to rebuttal by the imposing party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term permitting unilateral price changes without adequate justification is presumed to be unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term that permits one party to unilaterally alter prices or other material conditions of the contract without providing adequate justification is presumptively unfair, subject to rebuttal.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: The party that unilaterally imposed a contractual term bears the burden of proving it was subject to meaningful negotiation.
rule_text_technical: A term is deemed to have been unilaterally imposed where the party relying on it supplied the term without providing the other party with a genuine opportunity to influence its content; the burden of proving that a term was subject to meaningful negotiation lies with the supplying party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A public sector body may request private-sector data only where it is necessary to respond to a public emergency, the data is not otherwise obtainable, and it is genuinely necessary to fulfil a statutory public interest task.
rule_text_technical: Public sector bodies may request private data holders to make data available only where all of the following conditions are cumulatively met: (a) the data is necessary to respond to a public emergency; (b) the data holder has not made the data available on request; (c) the data cannot be obtained by other means on equivalent timelines and at equivalent cost; and (d) the data is genuinely necessary to fulfil a statutory task in the public interest.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Upon a valid public sector request, you must respond promptly and make data available through appropriate technical means.
rule_text_technical: Upon receipt of a valid request from a public sector body under Article 15, data holders must respond promptly and make the requested data available through appropriate technical means.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You may be compensated at cost for complying with a public sector data request, but compensation shall not exceed the direct costs of making the data available.
rule_text_technical: Data holders responding to public sector requests under Chapter V may receive compensation not exceeding the direct costs incurred in making the data available; no return on investment may be claimed.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Data provided to public sector bodies under this Chapter must not be used for commercial purposes or shared with third parties beyond the stated purpose.
rule_text_technical: Data made available to public sector bodies under Chapter V must not be used for commercial purposes and must not be shared with third parties beyond the purpose for which it was requested and obtained.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You must not impose and must actively remove commercial, technical, contractual, and organisational obstacles that prevent customers from switching data processing service providers.
rule_text_technical: Providers of data processing services must not impose, and must remove, any commercial, technical, contractual, or organisational obstacles that prevent customers from terminating contracts, signing with alternative providers, transferring exportable data and digital assets, achieving functional equivalence after migration, or separating bundled data processing services.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Switching-related contractual terms must be clearly set out in writing, permitting transitions without undue delay and within a maximum transitional period of 30 calendar days.
rule_text_technical: Contractual terms concerning switching must be clearly specified in writing and must include switching clauses permitting transitions to alternative providers without undue delay and within a maximum transitional period of 30 calendar days.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Your contract must not require a notice period exceeding two months for switching data processing services.
rule_text_technical: Contracts for data processing services must not impose a maximum notice period exceeding two months in relation to the customer's exercise of switching rights.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You must provide customers with at least a 30-calendar-day data retrieval period following the end of the transitional switching period.
rule_text_technical: Contracts must provide for a minimum 30-calendar-day period following the end of the transitional switching period during which the customer may retrieve all exportable data.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: After the data retrieval period, you must fully erase all exportable data of the customer.
rule_text_technical: Upon expiry of the data retrieval period following the end of the transitional period, the provider must fully erase all exportable data belonging to the customer.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: From 12 January 2027, you cannot impose any switching charges on customers.
rule_text_technical: With effect from 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services are prohibited from imposing any charges on customers in connection with the switching process.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Between 11 January 2024 and 12 January 2027, you may only impose reduced switching charges that do not exceed your direct costs linked to the switching process.
rule_text_technical: During the transitional period from 11 January 2024 to 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services may impose switching charges only to the extent that such charges do not exceed the direct costs linked to the switching process.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You must take all reasonable measures to enable functional equivalence for customers after switching to an alternative data processing service provider.
rule_text_technical: Providers of data processing services must take all reasonable measures to enable functional equivalence for customers following a switch to an alternative provider of equivalent data processing services.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Non-infrastructure providers must make open interfaces available at no cost and ensure compatibility with common interoperability specifications.
rule_text_technical: Providers of data processing services that are not infrastructure providers must make open interfaces available at no cost to customers and must ensure compatibility with common interoperability specifications applicable to their service category.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Where common interoperability specifications have not been published, you must export all exportable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format upon customer request.
rule_text_technical: In the absence of published common interoperability specifications, providers of data processing services must export all exportable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format upon request by the customer.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As an operator of a data space, you must provide a description of your data space through a single point of contact and implement technical specifications for data quality, portability, security, and governance.
rule_text_technical: Operators of data spaces must provide a description of their data space through a single point of contact and implement technical specifications addressing data quality, portability, security, and governance as essential requirements for interoperability.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Smart contracts used for data sharing must be robust and safe from unintended termination or interruption.
rule_text_technical: Smart contracts employed for the performance of data sharing obligations must be designed to be robust and resilient against unintended termination or interruption during execution.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Smart contracts used for data sharing must include access controls limiting operations to contractually specified parties.
rule_text_technical: Smart contracts used for data sharing obligations must incorporate access controls that restrict the execution of operations to parties specified under the applicable contractual terms.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Smart contracts used for data sharing must ensure data is stored, transmitted, and processed in compliance with applicable law.
rule_text_technical: Smart contracts used for data sharing obligations must ensure that data is stored, transmitted, and processed in a manner that is compliant with all applicable Union and national law.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Smart contracts used for data sharing must include mechanisms to terminate data processing and delete data upon instruction.
rule_text_technical: Smart contracts used for data sharing obligations must incorporate mechanisms enabling the termination of ongoing data processing operations and the deletion of data held under such contracts upon contractually specified instructions.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Smart contracts used for data sharing must include logging mechanisms to ensure traceability of all operations.
rule_text_technical: Smart contracts used for data sharing obligations must incorporate logging functionality sufficient to ensure the traceability of all operations performed under the contract.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Member States must establish penalties for infringements of this Regulation that are effective, proportionate, and dissuasive.
rule_text_technical: Member States are required to establish and maintain a system of penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation; such penalties must be effective, proportionate, and dissuasive, and maximum fines for legal persons must be established under national law.
